answer: A farm dies on arithmetic, and signed museum membership visit stamps with venue attestation is the arithmetic. A museum signs visit stamps showing the member attended on six different dates. A farm needs one real visitor per copy, and a membership with no visits has no trail to vouch for. Each identity carries its own vine, the lantern is never shared, and the quartz is bounded by the fact that the cost of the next copy is always the full cost of the first.
